new_statements.quote: Les tons : Nous pouvons relever en boomu trois tons ponctuels : bas ( \ ) pìn (accrocher à l'épaule) ; ʔò (plumer acc.) ; cà (croquer acc.) ; càn (prendre). moyen ( ) pin (décortiquer) ; ʔo (couper au niveau des racines (herbe)) ; ca (la trace) ; can (répondre). haut ( / ) pín (refuser) ; ʔó (mauvais) ; cá (gifler) ; cán (piocher). ainsi que l'existence de tons modulés sur voyelles courtes (notés par la succession de deux voyelles) : bas/haut ( V ) ɓὲέ (nég.) ; ʔòó-zo (poussin) ; còó (arracher). haut/bas ( / \ ) wéè (l'auxilaire d'habitude) ; dέdέὲ (petit à petit). bas/moyen ( \_ ) màa (voir acc.) ; nàa (vache (n. g.)) ; sàa (empêcher). haut/moyen ( /_ ) lée (sortir) ; lóo (village) ; báa (fleuve) ; sáa (mare). moyen/haut ( _/ ) mɛέ / mɛέnà (rester longtemps) ; seé (porter) ; leé (rappeler) ; laá (buffle).
new_statements.translation: Tones: we can identify in Boomu three level tones: low (\) pìn 'to hang on the shoulder'; ʔò 'to pluck (perf.)'; cà 'to crunch (perf.)'; càn 'to take'. mid ( ) pin 'to shell'; ʔo 'to cut grass at the roots'; ca 'the trace'; can 'to answer'. high (/) pín 'to refuse'; ʔó 'bad'; cá 'to slap'; cán 'to hoe'. as well as the existence of contour tones on short vowels (written as a sequence of two vowels): low/high ɓὲέ (neg.); ʔòó-zo 'chick'; còó 'to tear off'. high/low wéè (habitual auxiliary); dέdέὲ 'little by little'. low/mid màa 'to see (perf.)'; nàa 'cow'; sàa 'to prevent'. high/mid lée 'to go out'; lóo 'village'; báa 'river'; sáa 'pond'. mid/high mɛέ / mɛέnà 'to stay long'; seé 'to carry'; leé 'to remind'; laá 'buffalo'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Bomu (Boomu, Mandiakuy/dahanmu dialect, Mali) is described as a tone language with three lexically contrastive level tones (low, mid, high) on monosyllables plus five contour tones (LH, HL, LM, HM, MH) realised on short vowels; the source gives minimal triplets for the level tones. It says nothing about word stress or accent — no stress statement exists in any source opened.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the sketch notes only that dwemu (Togo dialect) speakers have tonal and lexical variants not always mastered by dahanmu speakers (p. 61), and Leguy's bibliography note on Manessy 1971 says the tonal scheme must take discourse prosody into account.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on citation-form monosyllabic words (verbs, nouns) in the Mandiakuy ('dahanmu') dialect of Mali; the thesis is an ethnolinguistic study of proverbs with a short grammatical sketch, not a full phonology.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes the Boomu of Mali, 'dialecte de Mandiakui' (dahanmu), the vehicular Bomu dialect of the San/Tominian area — the core of bomu1247 (no separate Glottolog dialect code known). Manessy 1960/1961 (Glottolog's refs for bomu1247) describe the Bondoukuy dialect on the Burkina side of the same language. The Burkina Bwamu phonologies in the Yé bibliography (Boni, Sanaba, Dédougou, Djibasso, Ouakara, bwamu laa) belong to the other Bwamu languages (bww/bwj/bwy), not to bomu1247.

No phonology; dialects Dahanmu (Mandiakuy), Dwemu (Togo), Mao; fr/de cite DNAFLA 1993 'Alphabets et règles d'orthographe des langues nationales', Bamako, pp. 19-21 (orthography: vowel length by doubling, nasalization by n).
